proposed.name: fixed-support minimax transition handle
proposed.construction: Within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), the support is the fixed known rectangle union \(H\) and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on \(H\), so a shrinking conditional-support hole is not an admissible path. Study minimax excess-endpoint risk along fixed-support sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), along which \(R(P)\to0\), by constructing and verifying Le Cam two-point or Assouad families of \(\beta\)-H\"older perturbations of \(g\) and/or \(\nu_P\) that preserve every class restriction and compatibility and separate the optimized endpoints of \(\Theta(P)\). A support-topology transition must instead be posed on a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class with explicit geometry and density conditions. This handle asserts no lower bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle must respect the corrected domain of \(R(P)\) and the compatibility restriction already required by the established uniform upper bound. This adds no lower-bound premise and leaves the least-favorable-family construction open.

proposed.statement: On the fixed known support \(H\) defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, along sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), along which \(R(P)\to0\)? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of estimating the obstacle boundary from the cost of estimating the signed objective? A shrinking support-hole transition lies outside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
proposed.justification: The upper rate becomes economically interpretable only after determining whether its obstacle and signed-objective terms are unavoidable along compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\).
proposed.gap: The known fixed rectangle support and uniform positive density lower bound exclude a shrinking support-hole transition from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Existing results provide neither a matching fixed-support lower bound over compatible laws nor a separately formalized varying-support class.
proposed.consumer: A matching fixed-support lower bound would show whether shorter uniformly honest sensitivity intervals require stronger functional restrictions or merely a better estimator; a support-topology claim must await a distinct class.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching minimax lower bound, uniform along fixed-support sequences in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\) and \(R(P)\to0\), that separately attributes endpoint loss to estimating the obstacle boundary and to estimating the signed objective; any support-topology transition additionally requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
obligation.obstruction: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is the same known finite rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) throughout \(H\). Hence the suggested shrinking-hole family is outside the frozen class. Within fixed \(H\), the primitives establish the upper bound but supply no verified two-point or hypercube family that simultaneously remains in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), preserves \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), has bounded product-experiment divergence, and separates an optimized WAOSS endpoint at the asserted rate.
obligation.attempted: The natural route perturbs \(g\) by a local \(\beta\)-H\"older bump and perturbs \(\nu_P\) to isolate the two error sources. A shrinking hole violates fixed support; on fixed support, verifying the density and outcome bounds, obstacle compatibility, divergence bound, and optimized-endpoint separation is precisely the missing least-favorable-family construction. Assuming those properties would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: The established theorem gives the uniform upper endpoint error \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\) over laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Also, \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is fixed and known and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on all of \(H\), so support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Thus the current minimax problem can let \(R(P)\to0\) only along compatible laws on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole lower bound belongs to a new varying-support class. No matching fixed-support lower bound or decomposition into obstacle and signed-objective costs follows from the frozen primitives.

Sharp identification regions under convex moment predictions supply general convex identified-region logic, not this continuum-to-mesh clipping and Hausdorff certificate.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set in nonparametric instrumental-variable models; this is not a WAOSS obstacle or endpoint result.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.

Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes; it does not characterize this partially identified WAOSS sensitivity frontier.

prose_updates.tldr: Marginal quasi-stayers do not identify the weighted WAOSS singleton claimed by de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): at a regular heterogeneous-baseline witness, the published completion class contains an affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is all of \(\mathbb R\). The positive result is instead a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure. Its completion class adds a finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, a continuous support version of \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline conditional-mean identity with a continuous baseline trend; the affine lifts satisfy both trend clauses. Marginal quasi-stayers are not required for this characterization, and its finite attained obstacle interval does not transfer to the unrestricted source class. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton formula; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 remains an analogous result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The finite outer program yields a uniformly honest interval on the fixed-support regular subclass, while minimaxity along compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\) remains open.

project_justification.gap: The proceedings paper states weighted WAOSS point identification under Assumptions 1--4, but marginal quasi-stayers do not imply the baseline-conditional positivity invoked immediately before display (4) of its Appendix proof. The regular witness gives a generic-class certificate of failure: the published completion class admits a legal affine recession ray whose WAOSS image is \(\mathbb R\). The source's per-dose parallel-trends clause also does not by itself justify substituting the random diagonal dose; the sensitivity model therefore retains that per-dose clause and separately imposes the realized-baseline identity \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)\), with \(m_Q\) a continuous version of the corresponding conditional mean given \(X\).
project_justification.niche: The paper separates three objects that cannot be conflated: the unrestricted published class, which is unbounded at the witness; a bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class with continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel trends, and a separate realized-baseline identity, which has an exact finite obstacle interval; and the baseline-conditional zero-support regime, in which that interval collapses to the published weighted formula. On source-admissible observed laws, only source completions also satisfying the added sensitivity restrictions are characterized; no global class equality or inclusion is asserted.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the source-class recession-ray counterexample and then characterizes the strengthened sensitivity class by a full-observed-law affine lift that satisfies both trend clauses, attained interval geometry, the exact criterion \(R(P)=0\) on the compatible domain, conditional-support singleton recovery, obstacle compatibility and constant-one clipping, certified finite programs, and uniform outer coverage on a fixed rectangle-support subclass. The common-zero-baseline scalar interval from arXiv:2405.04465v4 is retained solely as prior-art validation, and the source paper's separate parametric estimator is outside the challenge.

sampling_model.units: Each superpopulation unit has observed \(Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2\) and one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\). The sensitivity class retains the source's per-dose conditional-parallel-trends equality and separately requires \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)\) almost surely, where \(m_Q\) is an explicitly chosen continuous version of \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X]\). Realized-diagonal and period-two causal-movement integrability are imposed explicitly. The affine lifts satisfy the per-dose and realized-baseline clauses simultaneously.
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline and follow-up doses are continuous and exact stayers are excluded. The sensitivity sharpness theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the support version \(g\), and the separate realized-baseline identity in addition to the source's per-dose parallel trends. On an observed law satisfying the source assumptions, the reported finite interval concerns only completions satisfying these additional restrictions and does not transfer upward to the unrestricted source class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is combined with the signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program. The event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) yields uniform outer coverage and the proved excess-endpoint rate. A matching lower bound remains open for compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\); shrinking support holes require a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.

prose_updates.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix argument immediately before display (4)) state a weighted WAOSS singleton under marginal quasi-stayers, although the proof invokes baseline-conditional positivity. The accepted source-class recession-ray proposition shows that the issue is substantive: at the regular witness the published completion class generates every value in \(\mathbb R\). Only this non-representability result transfers directly to that class. The positive finite interval is a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure; it adds a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline identity with a continuous \(m_Q\). The affine lifts satisfy both trend clauses. Under baseline-conditional zero support the interval collapses to the proceedings paper's weighted formula. Section 4.1, Assumption 5, and Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 provide an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval of de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, arXiv:2405.04465v4, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2) is prior art used only as an algebraic sanity check. Andrews and Shi (2013) provide general conditional-moment-inequality inference, rather than the necessary-and-sufficient support-local obstacle certificate proved here. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011) develop convex sharp-region logic; Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) optimize weighted functionals under convex restrictions; and Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) obtain linear-program bounds on finite discrete support. Voronin (2025) studies values of programs that are already finite. None of those results supplies the exact clipping and Hausdorff certificate taking this continuum WAOSS class to a mesh. Freyberger (2017) studies completeness and consistency in nonparametric instrumental-variable models and data-driven bounds on identified-set diameter, not support-local WAOSS obstacles or endpoint inference. Sasaki and Ura (2025) develop bias correction and limit theory for point-identified slow-mover panel estimands, not this partially identified completion frontier. For inference, Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) establish uniform calibrated projection for finite moment systems, Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015) give uniform series-regression theory, and Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma (2024) give support-edge-adaptive conditional-density inference. The inference theorem makes no general advance in those component theories: for this WAOSS model it narrowly composes a primitive support-edge cell-mean band, a signed-measure band, the certified continuum discretization, a denominator band, and measurable ratio optimization. The proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated, and no current result supplies the open fixed-support minimax lower bound over compatible laws.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive identified set is exact only for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class, which retains the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition and separately imposes a realized-baseline identity with a continuous conditional-mean version. The inference theorem additionally fixes a known finite rectangle union, \(\beta\), a uniform positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation, and uses a conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed-measure control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation without density smoothness, strict feasibility, or optimizer uniqueness. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). A matching lower bound as \(R(P)\to0\) along compatible laws on fixed \(H\) remains open; shrinking-hole asymptotics require a new varying-support class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The negative conclusion is exact for the published class at the regular witness: its legal affine recession ray generates all of \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The finite set \(\Theta(P)\) is instead the sharp causal set for a strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class with a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline identity with a continuous \(m_Q\); the affine lifts satisfy both clauses. Marginal quasi-stayers are unnecessary for that sensitivity characterization. No global equality or inclusion with the source class is claimed, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 concerns unweighted \(\delta_1\); and the common-zero-baseline scalar bounds in arXiv:2405.04465v4 are prior art. The source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged. Uniform outer inference is confined to the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, density-bounded-below, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. No lower-bound optimality result is claimed; support-topology asymptotics, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length are also outside scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
By the declared support types, \(X_0\) is compact and \(H\) is a nonempty compact subset of \(I\times(I-I)\).  Moreover, if \((d,z)\in H\), then \(d\in X_0\).  Indeed, let \(U\) be any relative open neighborhood of \(d\) in \(I\), and let \(V\) be any relative open neighborhood of \(z\) in \(I-I\).  Since \((d,z)\in\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\),
\[
P\{(X,Z)\in U\times V\}>0.
\]
Therefore \(P(X\in U)>0\).  This holds for every such \(U\), so \(d\in\operatorname{supp}_P(X)=X_0\).

By \(\mathrm{ass:continuous\mbox{-}regression}\), \(g\) is continuous on the compact set \(H\), so there is a finite constant \(G_0\) such that \(|g(d,z)|\le G_0\) for every \((d,z)\in H\).  Compactness of \(I\) also bounds \(|z|\) and \(|x-d|\) on \(H\times X_0\).  Consequently, the supremum and infimum in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\) are finite at every \(x\in X_0\).

For each \((d,z)\in H\), introduce the functions
\[
a_{d,z}(x)=g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|,
\qquad
c_{d,z}(x)=g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|.
\]
For all \(x,x'\in X_0\), the reverse triangle inequality gives
\[
|a_{d,z}(x)-a_{d,z}(x')|
=L\bigl||x-d|-|x'-d|\bigr|
\le L|x-x'|,
\]
and the same bound holds for \(c_{d,z}\).  If every member \(f_j\) of a pointwise finite family is \(L\)-Lipschitz, then
\[
\sup_j f_j(x)-\sup_j f_j(x')
\le \sup_j\{f_j(x)-f_j(x')\}
\le L|x-x'|.
\]
Interchanging \(x\) and \(x'\) proves that \(\sup_j f_j\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.  Applying the same argument to \(-f_j\) proves the claim for a pointwise infimum.  Finally, the scalar maps \(v\mapsto\max\{-M,v\}\) and \(v\mapsto\min\{M,v\}\) are one-Lipschitz.  Therefore \(\ell_P\) and \(r_P\), as defined in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\), are finite-valued and \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(X_0\), and in particular belong to \(C(X_0)\).

We now prove the asserted class equality.  Let \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Fix \(x\in X_0\) and \((d,z)\in H\).  Since \(d\in X_0\), the Lipschitz and support-cone clauses of \(\mathrm{def:feasible\mbox{-}trend\mbox{-}class}\) give
\[
u(x)
\ge u(d)-L|x-d|
\ge g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|
=a_{d,z}(x).
\]
The level clause gives \(u(x)\ge -M\).  Taking the supremum over \((d,z)\in H\) and then the maximum with \(-M\) yields
\[
u(x)\ge \ell_P(x).
\]
Likewise,
\[
u(x)
\le u(d)+L|x-d|
\le g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|
=c_{d,z}(x),
\]
and \(u(x)\le M\).  Taking the infimum over \((d,z)\in H\) and then the minimum with \(M\) yields
\[
u(x)\le r_P(x).
\]
Because \(x\) was arbitrary and membership in \(\mathcal C_P\) already imposes continuity and Lipschitz constant at most \(L\), we obtain
\[
\mathcal C_P
\subseteq
\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,\ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}.
\]

Conversely, let \(u\in C(X_0)\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L\) and \(\ell_P\le u\le r_P\), where the inequalities are pointwise.  The outer truncations in \(\mathrm{def:obstacle\mbox{-}envelopes}\) imply
\[
\ell_P(x)\ge -M,
\qquad
r_P(x)\le M
\qquad (x\in X_0).
\]
Hence \(-M\le u(x)\le M\) for every \(x\in X_0\), so \(\|u\|_\infty\le M\).  For an arbitrary \((d,z)\in H\), evaluating the defining supremum and infimum at that same support point gives
\[
\ell_P(d)
\ge g(d,z)-K|z|-L|d-d|
=g(d,z)-K|z|
\]
and
\[
r_P(d)
\le g(d,z)+K|z|+L|d-d|
=g(d,z)+K|z|.
\]
Combining these inequalities with \(\ell_P(d)\le u(d)\le r_P(d)\) yields
\[
g(d,z)-K|z|\le u(d)\le g(d,z)+K|z|,
\]
or equivalently
\[
|g(d,z)-u(d)|\le K|z|.
\]
Thus \(u\) satisfies the level, Lipschitz, and support-cone clauses of \(\mathrm{def:feasible\mbox{-}trend\mbox{-}class}\), and therefore \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  This proves
\[
\mathcal C_P
=
\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,\ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}.
\]

If \(\mathcal C_P\ne\varnothing\), choose \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  The class equality just proved gives
\[
\ell_P(x)\le u(x)\le r_P(x)
\qquad\text{for every }x\in X_0,
\]
so \(\ell_P\le r_P\) pointwise.  Conversely, suppose \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).  Set \(u=\ell_P\).  The first part of the proof shows that \(u\in C(X_0)\) and \(\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L\); the assumed order gives \(\ell_P\le u\le r_P\).  The established class equality then implies \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Hence \(\mathcal C_P\ne\varnothing\), completing both directions of the compatibility criterion.

Because the declared observed law \(P\) is supported on \(\mathbb R^2\times I^2\) and \(I\) is compact,
\[
|Z|=|D_2-D_1|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)
\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The no-stayer condition gives \(|Z|>0\) almost surely, and hence
\[
0<A=E_P|Z|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty. \tag{1}
\]
Observed integrability gives
\[
E_P|\Delta Y|\leq E_P(|Y_1|+|Y_2|)<\infty.
\]
Since \(|S|=1\) almost surely under the no-stayer condition,
\[
|T|=|E_P[S\Delta Y]|\leq E_P|\Delta Y|<\infty. \tag{2}
\]
Thus all ratios used below have a finite, strictly positive denominator.

Take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), and abbreviate
\[
B_Q=Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1),
\qquad
C_Q=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1).
\]
The two variables are integrable by the explicit realized-diagonal and causal-movement requirements in \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\). Consistency and the observed-law match give
\[
\Delta Y=C_Q+B_Q
\qquad Q\text{-almost surely}. \tag{3}
\]
The separate realized-baseline identity gives directly, without substituting a random dose into the per-dose parallel-trends condition,
\[
E_Q[B_Q\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)
\qquad Q\text{-almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]
Because \(Q\) matches the complete observed law \(P\), the declared support version \(g\) is also a version of \(E_Q[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\). Taking conditional expectations in (3), using linearity for the integrable summands and then (4), yields
\[
E_Q[C_Q\mid X,Z]=g(X,Z)-m_Q(X)
\qquad Q\text{-almost surely}. \tag{5}
\]
The mean-movement bound therefore implies
\[
|g(x,z)-m_Q(x)|\leq K|z|
\qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}. \tag{6}
\]
The function
\[
(x,z)\longmapsto |g(x,z)-m_Q(x)|-K|z|
\]
is continuous on \(H\): \(g\in C(H)\), and the continuous-version condition gives \(m_Q\in C(X_0)\). If this function were positive at some \((x_0,z_0)\in H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), continuity would make it positive on the intersection of \(H\) with an open neighborhood of \((x_0,z_0)\). By the definition of support that neighborhood has positive \(P_{XZ}\)-probability, contradicting (6). Hence
\[
|g(x,z)-m_Q(x)|\leq K|z|
\qquad\text{for every }(x,z)\in H. \tag{7}
\]
The level and global Lipschitz restrictions on \(m_Q\) are also member conditions of \(\mathfrak Q(P)\). Comparing them and (7) with \(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) proves
\[
m_Q\in\mathcal C_P. \tag{8}
\]
In particular, \(\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\) implies \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\).

We next derive the causal-functional relationship. By the causal definition of \(\theta(Q)\), equation (3), the bounded \((X,Z)\)-measurable variable \(S\), equation (4), and iterated expectations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
A\theta(Q)
&=E_Q[SC_Q]\\
&=E_P[S\Delta Y]-E_Q[SB_Q]\\
&=T-E_Q\!\left[S E_Q[B_Q\mid X,Z]\right]\\
&=T-E_P[Sm_Q(X)].
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(v\) on \(X_0\), the definition
\(\nu_P(B)=E_P[S\mathbf 1\{X\in B\}]\), first for simple functions and then by bounded convergence, gives
\[
\int_{X_0}v(x)\,d\nu_P(x)=E_P[Sv(X)]. \tag{10}
\]
Applying (10) to the bounded continuous function \(m_Q\), and then using \(\text{def:signed-functional}\), turns (9) into
\[
\theta(Q)=\frac{T-J_P(m_Q)}{A}. \tag{11}
\]
Equations (8) and (11), followed by \(\text{def:waoss-set}\), prove
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}\subseteq\Theta(P). \tag{12}
\]

For the reverse inclusion, fix arbitrary \(u\in\mathcal C_P\). Retain the observed vector on its \(P\)-probability space. On \(\{Z\neq0\}\), define
\[
b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z},
\]
and put \(b_u=0\) on the null event \(\{Z=0\}\). The construction is measurable, and the support obstacle in \(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) gives
\[
|b_u|\leq K
\qquad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{13}
\]
For every \(d\in I\), define the affine schedules from \(\text{def:affine-lift}\):
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2). \tag{14}
\]
They are jointly measurable in the random argument and \(d\). At the realized doses,
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2. \tag{15}
\]
Thus the complete observed law remains \(P\), and consistency holds. For each fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\), (13), and observed integrability imply
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
\qquad
E_{Q_u}|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|<\infty. \tag{16}
\]
Moreover, for \(d,d'\in I\),
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|
=|b_u|\,|d-d'|
\leq K|d-d'|, \tag{17}
\]
so each period schedule is individually \(K\)-Lipschitz.

Direct subtraction in (14) gives, pointwise off \(\{Z=0\}\) and simultaneously for all \(d\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
&=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
&=\Delta Y-b_uZ\\
&=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X).
\end{aligned} \tag{18}
\]
The right side is integrable because
\[
E_P|g(X,Z)|
\leq E_P\!\left[E_P(|\Delta Y|\mid X,Z)\right]
=E_P|\Delta Y|<\infty
\]
and \(|u(X)|\leq M\). Since \(g(X,Z)\) is a version of \(E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\), (18) gives, for every fixed \(d\in I\),
\[
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]=u(X). \tag{19}
\]
Taking the conditional expectation of (19) given \(X\) gives
\[
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]=u(X). \tag{20}
\]
Thus (19)--(20) verify the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition. In fact, because the random difference in (18) is independent of \(d\), the displayed versions can be chosen identically for every \(d\in I\); this stronger fact is a property derived for the lift, not an assumption used to evaluate a random diagonal.

Taking \(d=D_1=X\) in the pointwise schedule identity (18), rather than in a fixed-dose conditional-expectation statement, gives
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)-Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)
=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X). \tag{21}
\]
Its integrability was proved above. Conditioning (21) on \((X,Z)\) and on \(X\), respectively, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)-Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]&=u(X),\\
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)-Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X]&=u(X).
\end{aligned} \tag{22}
\]
Because \(u\in C(X_0)\), equation (22) proves both that \(m_{Q_u}=u\) is a continuous version and that the separate realized-baseline identity holds. Its level and global \(L\)-Lipschitz restrictions follow from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).

The realized period-two causal movement is
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)
=b_uZ=g(X,Z)-u(X). \tag{23}
\]
By feasibility and bounded treatment support,
\[
|g(X,Z)-u(X)|\leq K|Z|leq K\operatorname{diam}(I), \tag{24}
\]
so the movement is integrable. Since it is \((X,Z)\)-measurable, (24) also gives
\[
\left|E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|
=|g(X,Z)-u(X)|
\leq K|Z|. \tag{25}
\]
Equations (13)--(25) verify every member condition in \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\). Therefore
\[
Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P), \tag{26}
\]
which also proves \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\).

Finally, the causal definition, (23), and iterated expectations give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta(Q_u)
&=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}\\
&=\frac{E_P[S\Delta Y]-E_P[Su(X)]}{A}\\
&=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\end{aligned} \tag{27}
\]
where the second equality uses \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]\) and the third uses (10). Since \(u\) was arbitrary, (26)--(27) prove \(\Theta(P)\subseteq\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}\). Combined with (12), this proves the sharp set equality and full-law attainment.

No step uses marginal quasi-stayers. The forward direction uses the realized-baseline identity directly; the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition is retained as a class restriction but is not misused to justify a random-diagonal substitution. The affine lifts satisfy both clauses, as (19)--(22) show. The finite movement bound, bounded globally Lipschitz trend, continuous support version of \(g\), explicit integrability conditions, and realized-baseline identity remain additional sensitivity restrictions. Therefore the equality proved here characterizes \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) only and does not transfer the finite interval to the unrestricted published completion class.

The first rectangle in \(\text{def:continuous-hole-witness}\) has area \(1/2\) and density \(2p_{\circ}\), hence probability \(p_{\circ}\). The second rectangle also has area \(1/2\) and density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\), hence probability \(1-p_{\circ}\). Since \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the density is bounded and has a strictly positive constant value on each rectangle. The observed outcomes are identically zero and are therefore uniformly bounded. Absolute continuity gives
\[
P^{\circ}(Z=0)=0. \tag{28}
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), the intersection of the second rectangle with \(\{|z|\leq\eta\}\) has positive Lebesgue measure. Its density is positive, so
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta)>0. \tag{29}
\]
Thus marginal quasi-stayers are verified directly by the witness; no marginal quasi-stayer assumption is a premise of this proposition. In contrast, for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), the conditional support of \(Z\) is \([1/2,1]\), and hence
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta\mid X=x)=0
\qquad(0<\eta<1/2). \tag{30}
\]
The first-rectangle marginal density of \(X\) is \(p_{\circ}\) on \([-1,0]\), so the set in (30) has \(P_X^{\circ}\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\).

Fix finite \(c\in\mathbb R\) and take \(Q_c^{\circ}\) from \(\text{def:source-recession-ray}\). On the first rectangle, \(|\phi(X)|\leq1/2\leq|Z|\), while on the second rectangle \(\phi(X)=0\). Therefore, outside the null event in (28),
\[
\left|\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\right|\leq |c|. \tag{31}
\]
Because \(D_1,D_2,d\in[-2,2]\), each schedule is bounded in absolute value by \(4|c|\) for every fixed \(d\). It is thus integrable and affine in \(d\), with everywhere finite derivative \(-c\phi(X)/Z\). At the realized doses,
\[
Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)=0=Y_2. \tag{32}
\]
Hence consistency holds and the entire observed vector retains law \(P^{\circ}\).

For every \(d\in[-2,2]\), direct subtraction gives on the same event for all \(d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)
&=-\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\{(d-D_2)-(d-X)\}\\
&=c\phi(X).
\end{aligned} \tag{33}
\]
The right side is measurable with respect to \(X\). Consequently one may choose versions, simultaneously for every \(d\in[-2,2]\), such that
\[
E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X,Z]
=c\phi(X)
=E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X]. \tag{34}
\]
This verifies the per-dose parallel-trends restriction in \(\text{def:published-source-completion-class}\), and indeed the stronger all-dose version. Equations (31)--(34), together with the support properties, prove
\[
Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})
\qquad\text{for every finite }c. \tag{35}
\]

The realized period-two causal movement is
\[
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=-c\phi(X). \tag{36}
\]
On the first rectangle \(S=1\); on the second, \(\phi(X)=0\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]
&=p_{\circ}\int_{-1}^{0}\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx\\
&=\frac{3p_{\circ}}8.
\end{aligned} \tag{37}
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|
&=p_{\circ}E[Z\mid Z\in[1/2,1]]
 +(1-p_{\circ})E[|Z|\mid Z\in[-1/4,1/4]]\\
&=\frac{3p_{\circ}}4+\frac{1-p_{\circ}}8
=\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8>0.
\end{aligned} \tag{38}
\]
The causal definition of \(\theta\), together with (36)--(38), yields
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})
=-\frac{cE_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]}{E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|}
=-\frac{3cp_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}. \tag{39}
\]
Because the coefficient of \(c\) is nonzero and every finite \(c\) gives a legal source completion by (35), the source-class image contains \(\mathbb R\). Conversely, the source class requires integrability of the movement entering \(\theta\), and (38) gives a positive denominator, so every value of \(\theta(Q)\) is a finite real number. Therefore
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}=\mathbb R. \tag{40}
\]

For the bounded-sensitivity calculation, \(\Delta Y=0\) under \(P^{\circ}\), so \(g=0\) is a continuous conditional-mean support version. Set \(K=L=M=1\). For every \(u\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\), the points \((x,0)\in H\) for \(x\in[0,1]\) imply
\[
|u(x)|=|g(x,0)-u(x)|\leq |0|=0,
\]
and therefore \(u=0\) on \([0,1]\). In particular \(u(0)=0\). For \(x\in[-1,0]\), the support point \((x,1/2)\) gives \(|u(x)|\leq1/2\), while global one-Lipschitz continuity and \(u(0)=0\) give \(|u(x)|\leq -x\). Thus
\[
|u(x)|\leq\phi(x)
\qquad(x\in[-1,1]). \tag{41}
\]
Both \(\phi\) and \(-\phi\) are continuous, bounded by one, and globally one-Lipschitz. On the first rectangle their absolute value is at most \(1/2\leq|z|\), and on the second they vanish. Hence
\[
\phi,-\phi\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}. \tag{42}
\]

On the first rectangle \(S=1\). On the second, conditional symmetry of \(Z\) gives \(E[S\mid X]=0\). Therefore
\[
d\nu_{P^{\circ}}(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx. \tag{43}
\]
Equations (37), (41)--(43) imply
\[
-\frac{3p_{\circ}}8
\leq J_{P^{\circ}}(u)
\leq\frac{3p_{\circ}}8, \tag{44}
\]
with the lower and upper values attained by \(-\phi\) and \(\phi\), respectively. Here \(T=0\), and (38) gives \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\). The full-law sharpness theorem and the already established attained-interval theorem therefore yield
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})=
\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
       \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right]. \tag{45}
\]
The definitions give \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\). Equation (39) shows that these laws attain the lower and upper endpoints, respectively. As affine lifts, they satisfy both the per-dose condition and the separate realized-baseline identity; this also follows directly from (33)--(34), because the realized baseline contrast is \(c\phi(X)\).

Finally, if baseline-conditional zero support holds, then \((x,0)\in H\) for every relevant \(x\). The obstacle defining \(\mathcal C_P\) gives
\[
|g(x,0)-u(x)|\leq K|0|=0,
\]
so every feasible trend satisfies \(u(x)=g(x,0)\). Substitution into \(\text{def:waoss-set}\) gives the singleton
\[
\left\{\frac{T-\int_{X_0}g(x,0)\,d\nu_P(x)}{A}\right\}. \tag{46}
\]
Thus the source class gives all of \(\mathbb R\) at this witness, the explicit bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class gives (45), and conditional zero support gives (46). Only the failure of the source singleton transfers to the unrestricted source class; the finite sensitivity interval does not.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the declared observed-law conditions, the source's per-dose conditional-parallel-trends condition, and the separate realized-baseline identity, the bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty,
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P).
\]
For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, on one common full-probability event,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)
\qquad\text{for every }d\in I.
\]
Consequently the lift satisfies the per-dose parallel-trends condition for every fixed dose and, separately, the realized-baseline identity; in fact its displayed equality yields common versions for all \(d\in I\). It also satisfies \(\theta(Q_u)=\{T-J_P(u)\}/A\). This theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model is not the class defined by Assumptions 1--4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): the theorem additionally imposes realized-diagonal and movement integrability, the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the observed regression version \(g\), and the explicit realized-baseline identity. Thus no equality or global inclusion of the two observed-law models is asserted. On an observed law that satisfies the published assumptions, \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is only the restricted slice satisfying these extra conditions, and \(\Theta(P)\) is not asserted to be the published-class identified set. The result is a sharp bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity repair after failure of the published singleton claim, not a sharp characterization of the unrestricted published class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current common-event fixed-dose clause does not by itself justify evaluating conditional-expectation versions at the random dose \(d=X\). The corrected claim retains the source's per-dose condition and separately assumes the realized-baseline conditional-mean identity, with explicit diagonal and movement integrability. This narrows the premise exactly where the original proof was invalid while preserving the sharp-set and affine-attainment conclusions.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
On the domain \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), define
\[
V_P^-=\inf_{u\in\mathcal C_P}J_P(u),\qquad
V_P^+=\sup_{u\in\mathcal C_P}J_P(u),\qquad
R(P)=V_P^+-V_P^-.
\]

The attained-interval theorem later upgrades these values to a minimum and maximum.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), the support is the fixed known rectangle union \(H\) and \(f_{XZ}\geq f_0>0\) on \(H\), so a shrinking conditional-support hole is not an admissible path. Study minimax excess-endpoint risk only along compatible fixed-support sequences: every law \(P\) in the sequence must satisfy \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), and along the sequence \(R(P)\to0\). Construct and verify Le Cam two-point or Assouad families of \(\beta\)-H\"older perturbations of \(g\) and/or \(\nu_P\) that preserve every class restriction and separate the optimized endpoints of \(\Theta(P)\). A support-topology transition must instead be posed on a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class with explicit geometry and density conditions. This handle asserts no lower bound.

proposed.name: bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\)
proposed.construction:
The bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class is
\[
\mathfrak Q(P)=\left\{Q:\begin{array}{l}
Q\text{ is a law over the declared one-argument static schedules on }I
\text{ and matches the entire observed law }P;\\
\text{consistency and fixed-dose latent integrability hold, and }g\in C(H);\\
Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\text{ and }Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\text{ are integrable};\\
\text{for every fixed }d\in X_0\text{, the per-dose conditional-parallel-trends equality holds};\\
E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X]\text{ admits the continuous version }m_Q(X);\\
E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)\quad Q\text{-almost surely};\\
\left|E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|\leq K|Z|quad Q\text{-almost surely};\\
\|m_Q\|_\infty\leq M,\quad
|m_Q(x)-m_Q(x')|\leq L|x-x'|\quad\text{for all }x,x'\in X_0
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
No marginal quasi-stayer restriction is part of this definition. The source's per-dose parallel-trends condition is retained without a common-event strengthening. The realized-baseline identity is imposed separately and is not obtained by substituting \(d=X\) into that fixed-dose condition. Realized-diagonal and causal-movement integrability, the finite \(K\) movement bound, the bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trend, and the continuous support version \(g\) are explicit sensitivity restrictions. On an observed law satisfying the published assumptions, comparison with the source class concerns only source completions that also satisfy these additional restrictions. No global equality or inclusion of completion classes is asserted, and the finite sharp interval for this sensitivity class does not transfer upward to the unrestricted published class.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\) be the published Assumptions 1--4 completion class and let \(Q_c^{\circ}\) be the affine completion generated by \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(\phi\). The law \(P^{\circ}\) has a bounded density that is strictly positive on each rectangle of its finite rectangle support and has uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies marginal quasi-stayers, whereas baseline-conditional positivity fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a region of \(P^{\circ}_X\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\). For every finite \(c\), \(Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\), its schedules are affine and integrable, it preserves the entire observed law, and it satisfies parallel trends simultaneously for every \(d\in[-2,2]\). Moreover,
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})=-\frac{3c p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\qquad
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}=\mathbb R.
\]
For the strengthened sensitivity class with \(K=L=M=1\), \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\) attain the endpoints
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})=
\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
       \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
Thus the identification elbow has three distinct stages: the unrestricted published class gives all of \(\mathbb R\) at this regular witness; the bounded-slope/Lipschitz class gives the displayed finite obstacle interval; and, under baseline-conditional zero support, the obstacle restriction fixes \(u(x)=g(x,0)\) and yields the published weighted singleton formula. Only the negative conclusion for the published singleton transfers to the published class; the finite interval does not.
proposed.justification: The affine recession ray proves that the published-class failure is unbounded, while the bounded-slope/Lipschitz model has a finite sharp interval.
proposed.gap: Marginal quasi-stayers do not supply the baseline-conditional support used before display (4) in the proof of the published theorem; the regular witness makes the resulting source-class identified set equal to \(\mathbb R\).
proposed.consumer: The result separates the invalid published singleton, the finite sensitivity interval under explicit bounds, and recovery of the weighted singleton under conditional zero support.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The witness proves marginal quasi-stayers directly, so depending on the marginal quasi-stayer assumption is circular and unnecessary. The mathematical claim is unchanged, and its revised proof is supplied separately.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula; the regular witness shows that this singleton is not identified over that published class.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design; that scalar prior result is not claimed as novel here.

Andrews and Shi (2013) develop inference based on conditional moment inequalities; they do not provide this model's necessary-and-sufficient support-local obstacle compatibility certificate or its full-law affine attainment argument.
Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011) provide convex sharp-identification-region logic; they do not supply the present continuum obstacle clipping and certified mesh-Hausdorff map for WAOSS.
Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) obtain sharp bounds from finite linear programs under discrete-support shape restrictions; they do not provide the continuum-to-mesh clipping certificate used here.

Freyberger (2017) shows that data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of an identified set in nonparametric instrumental-variable models; it does not establish this panel obstacle identified set or its WAOSS endpoint program.
Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) optimize policy-relevant weighted functionals under convex restrictions on marginal treatment effects; they do not derive this conditional-completion frontier.

Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) obtain uniformly valid calibrated projection for finite moment-inequality systems; the present inference theorem separately constructs the boundary-cell and continuum-discretization ingredients for this WAOSS model.
Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015) provide uniform series-regression theory; they do not give the signed-measure, obstacle-program, and ratio composition specialized here.
Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma (2024) provide boundary-adaptive conditional-density inference; they do not supply the present primitive boundary-cell conditional-mean band or WAOSS program.

Sasaki and Ura (2025) study panel estimands and inference with slow movers; that work does not establish the full-law sharp WAOSS completion set or repair the baseline-conditional support gap proved here.
